title: Which has eight legs?
hook: Spiders and insects share a broader animal group.

doesNotKnow: Distinguish a spider and an insect using adult leg count.

misconception: Every arthropod with jointed legs is an insect.
objective: Distinguish a spider and an insect using adult leg count.

claims.text: Spiders and insects share a broader animal group. In the pictured adult examples, which animal has four pairs of legs? The schematic spider has four pairs of legs; the insect has three pairs. Both are arthropods, but spiders are arachnids rather than insects. These simple drawings omit many anatomical details.
claims.source: Source leads for independent checking: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, https://naturalhistory.si.edu/research/entomology; OpenStax Biology 2e, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/28-3-superphylum-ecdysozoa. The precise supporting passages have not been checked.

claims.text: The stage uses a simplified, not-to-scale schematic and stated model assumptions; it is not a photographic observation of an individual animal.
Recall: A typical adult spider has four pairs of legs. How many legs is that? Four pairs contain eight legs.
